rationale: Interpret the completed execution of the Node-wrapper basis (CheckRun c53145c01ad94b449ca1c8b81fe8d7b4, fixed experiment 2318a1c9ee5d4b76995a322bd4bfcf06-experiment, version 3): all nine comparisons resolved - two controls hold, two premises hold on the witness event, the two witness assertions are violated, and the three restore comparisons hold. The question's two discriminator items are therefore both measured: the channel is closed after the re-add with the leadership unchanged, and it re-opens once the leadership changes. The restore path moves from a limitation to a measured bound, the question's discriminator is replaced by the remaining open point (how a caller can detect the closed channel), and the earlier receipts stay as history.

investigations.discriminator: Whether an application can detect the closed proposal channel other than through its own context deadline (the wrapper returns no error and no distinct signal), and whether other configuration sequences reach the same state (for example a re-add whose change is applied before the node's own Progress entry is dropped).

interpretations.rationale: The account is complete on one receipt whose prefix honours the application's duties. Source side: node.run sets its proposal channel to nil when an applied configuration change removes the local node from Progress and the node appears in neither cs.Voters nor cs.VotersOutgoing (node.go:400-432), restores the channel from n.propc only in the branch that reacts to a change of r.lead with a leader known (node.go:343-380), and Node.Propose sends into that channel, so a nil channel makes the call wait for the caller's context or the node's done channel (node.go:514-551); the target's own comment calls this reset unsound (node.go:409-411) and the only documented caveat is that proposals can be lost without notice (node.go:138-140). Receipt c53145c01ad94b449ca1c8b81fe8d7b4 (seven parsed events, no loss, nine comparisons all resolved) shows the whole arc on a conforming prefix: the wrapped node applies the bootstrap entry, the removal and the re-add in order (applied/committed 1, 2, 3, 4 while the leader's configuration moves voters=(1 2) -> voters=(1) -> voters=(1 2)) with the same term and the same known leader. Controls: before the removal Propose returns no error in 0ms and the leader's log index is 2 (parsed index 1, both comparisons hold), so the wrapper forwards a follower's proposal to the group. Witness: after the re-add, with the leader's configuration containing node 2 again (premise holds at parsed index 4) and the node still knowing leader 1 (premise holds), Propose returns only when its 300ms deadline fires and the leader's log index stays at 4 (both witness comparisons violated with a complete witness). Restore: the wrapped node then campaigns and reports itself as leader at term 2 (parsed index 5, comparison holds), the same Propose call returns no error in 0ms and its own commit index advances from 5 to 6 (parsed index 6, both comparisons hold), so the channel re-opens exactly when the leadership changes - which is the only mechanism the source provides and which does not occur while the same leader stays in place. The defect statement: a node that the application has added back to the configuration, and that knows the leader of that configuration in the same term, cannot hand a proposal to raft through the Node interface; the wrapper holds the call until the caller's context expires, the group never sees the proposal, and the fault disappears only after a leadership change (or by the application using another path such as RawNode, which has no such channel). Earlier receipts are history: 8b3e88d4b4a641fa8ddc723ecc0ba56d had a prefix that omitted the persistence duty and is withdrawn as evidence, and 4dc33f26f12e4cd69f7aae09af6c1ee6 measured the control, premises and witness on the corrected prefix but not the restore path.

knowledge.assertion: The proposal channel is closed by the removal guard and restored only by a leadership change with a leader known.
With a nil proposal channel Propose blocks until the caller's context or the node's done channel fires.

counterevidence: The controls hold in this receipt (parsed index 1): the same call before the removal returns no error and the leader's log index advances, so the blocked behaviour is specific to the state after the removal and the re-add rather than a general property of the wrapper or the harness.

The restore comparisons hold (parsed indices 5 and 6): after the leadership changes the call succeeds and the group sees the proposal, so the fault is bounded by the leadership rather than permanent, and the source's stated repair mechanism is confirmed by measurement.

The Node.Propose documentation warns that proposals can be lost without notice and that retries are the caller's job (node.go:138-140), so a caller with a deadline and retries is not blocked; what the warning does not describe is a member that is registered again and knows the leader yet cannot propose until the leadership changes.

The earlier receipt whose prefix omitted the application's persistence duty is withdrawn as evidence; the behaviour reproduced unchanged on the corrected prefix, so the correction did not create or remove the behaviour.
limitations: The harness drives a wrapped node against a bare raft instance, so the wrapper's asynchronous ready/advance contract is exercised on one side only, and both nodes run in one process; the leader is installed directly before the removal and the campaign is driven through the wrapper's own Campaign.

The proposed calls use a 300ms deadline: the receipt measures that the call did not complete within it and that the group's log did not change, not the exact duration of the closed channel; the source supports that it stays closed until the leadership changes, and the restore comparisons show the change is sufficient.

The two-voter group is the only configuration exercised for this question; whether other membership sequences (a demotion to learner, a re-add applied before the node's own entry is dropped, or a larger group) reach the same closed state is not measured.

Whether an application is expected to keep proposing through a node that has been removed and re-added is itself part of the question; the library's own comment calls the mechanism unsound rather than documenting an intended semantics.
